items.problem: UWP in-process App Service *provider* activation does not map to WinAppSDK: ExtendedActivationKind has no AppService member (CS0117) and Windows.ApplicationModel.Activation.IAppServiceActivatedEventArgs does not exist (CS0234). The dev-agent tried to port the provider branch and had to strip it after a failed build.
items.evidence: session-log.txt:2797 (CS0117 ExtendedActivationKind.AppService), :2798 (CS0234 IAppServiceActivatedEventArgs), :2858 (agent deletes the provider activation branch from App.xaml.cs).
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md '## Application Lifecycle and Activation' (line ~317) documents AppInstance.GetCurrent().GetActivatedEventArgs() and lists ExtendedActivationKind.File/Protocol/AppNotification cases — but says nothing about which kinds are absent, and never mentions App Services.
items.proposed_improvement: In the activation section, add a callout that ExtendedActivationKind covers only supported kinds (no AppService), that IAppServiceActivatedEventArgs is unavailable, that provider-side app-service activation must be removed or hosted out-of-process, and that the client side (AppServiceConnection) still works with package identity.
items.generalizes: App Services are a common UWP inter-app/background pattern; any sample or app that implements an app-service provider hits the same missing ExtendedActivationKind.AppService / IAppServiceActivatedEventArgs wall on WinAppSDK. Documenting the unsupported provider path and the client-vs-provider split prevents wasted build cycles across scenarios.
